options.label: Layer height
options.tooltip: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time

options.label: Initial layer height
options.tooltip: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhension

options.label: Mixed color sublayer
options.tooltip: Enable splitting each mixed-filament layer into sub-layers for physical colour blending. Requires at least one enabled mixed filament row.

options.label: Default
options.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Initial layer
options.tooltip: Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Outer wall
options.tooltip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Inner wall
options.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Top surface
options.tooltip: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Sparse infill
options.tooltip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Internal solid infill
options.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Support
options.tooltip: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

options.label: Seam position
options.tooltip: The start position to print each part of outer wall

options.label: Staggered inner seams
options.tooltip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

options.label: Seam gap
options.tooltip:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

options.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
options.tooltip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

options.label: Conditional scarf joint
options.tooltip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

options.label: Conditional angle threshold
options.tooltip:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

options.label: Conditional overhang threshold
options.tooltip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

options.label: Scarf joint speed
options.tooltip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s).  It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

options.label: Scarf start height
options.tooltip:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

options.label: Scarf around entire wall
options.tooltip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

options.label: Scarf length
options.tooltip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

options.label: Scarf steps
options.tooltip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

options.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
options.tooltip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

options.label: Role base wipe speed
options.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role.e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

options.label: Wipe speed
options.tooltip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration.If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above.The default value for this parameter is 80%

options.label: Wipe on loops
options.tooltip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

options.label: Wipe before external loop
options.tooltip:
To minimise visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the deretraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface. 

This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely an external perimeter is printed immediately after a deretraction move.

options.label: Slice gap closing radius
options.tooltip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

options.label: Resolution
options.tooltip: G-code path is genereated after simplifing the contour of model to avoid too much points and gcode lines in gcode file. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice

options.label: Arc fitting
options.tooltip: Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

options.label: X-Y hole compensation
options.tooltip: Holes of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes holes bigger. Negative value makes holes smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

options.label: X-Y contour compensation
options.tooltip: Contour of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes contour bigger. Negative value makes contour smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

options.label: Elephant foot compensation
options.tooltip: Shrink the initial layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect

options.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
options.tooltip: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

options.label: Precise wall
options.tooltip:
Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency.
Note: This setting will only take effect if the wall sequence is configured to Inner-Outer

options.label: Convert holes to polyholes
options.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

options.label: Polyhole detection margin
options.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

options.label: Polyhole twist
options.tooltip: Rotate the polyhole every layer.

options.label: Precise Z height
options.tooltip: Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

options.label: Enable Z-layer anti-aliasing
options.tooltip:
Consider enabling Z-layer anti-aliasing for models with large, gently sloped surfaces to reduce visible stair-stepping. For the best possible surface finish, consider using concentric top-surface fill.
When enabled, eligible top-surface and wall paths adjust their Z height to follow the model surface. Z-layer anti-aliasing is mutually exclusive with Spiral vase, Scarf joint seam, and Mixed color sublayer. Z-layer anti-aliasing cannot be enabled together with any of these features. Objects using a raft or ironing, or containing negative parts, fall back to conventional midplane slicing and display a warning. When this feature is enabled, arc commands in eligible paths are converted into G1 linear moves.

options.label: Minimum surface slope for wall lowering
options.tooltip:
Sets the minimum slope for additional wall lowering, applied only to paths that pass the Z-layer anti-aliasing filter. The eligible slope range varies with layer height. Values that are too high may have no effect. Set to 0 to disable this compensation.

For example, with a 0.20 mm layer height and a 0.42 mm outer-wall line width, values of 35° or higher generally produce no additional lowering. The 35° value is not a fixed upper limit.

options.label: ZAA slice-plane offset
options.tooltip:
Sets the Z offset of the slicing plane relative to the bottom of each layer, affecting the dynamic layer thickness. When set to 0, the system automatically selects a suitable offset based on the layer height, including adaptive layer heights. The first layer is always sliced at its midplane.

A larger value allows less downward adjustment and more upward adjustment of paths, increasing the risk of interference with higher paths. Keeping the default value is recommended.

options.label: Lock top-surface fill direction
options.tooltip: Keeps the direction of non-bridge, line-based top-surface fill patterns (such as Rectilinear and Monotonic) unchanged between layers when Z-layer anti-aliasing is active for the current object. Bridge fill direction and other fill types are unaffected.

options.label: Ironing Type
options.tooltip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed

options.label: Ironing Pattern
options.tooltip: The pattern that will be used when ironing

options.label: Ironing speed
options.tooltip: Print speed of ironing lines

options.label: Ironing flow
options.tooltip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface

options.label: Ironing line spacing
options.tooltip: The distance between the lines of ironing

options.label: Ironing angle
options.tooltip: The angle ironing is done at. A negative number disables this function and uses the default method.

options.label: Wall generator
options.tooltip: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width

options.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
options.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude

options.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
options.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

options.label: Wall transition length
options.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

options.label: Wall distribution count
options.tooltip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width

options.label: First layer minimum wall width
options.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

options.label: Minimum wall width
options.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

options.label: Minimum feature size
options.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

options.label: Minimum wall length
options.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the ouside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visibile if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

options.label: Walls printing order
options.tooltip:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls. 

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recomended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases. 

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

Use Adaptive Outer/Inner to combine the strengths of both the Outer/Inner and Inner/Outer print sequences. In most situations, this mode will print the outer wall first. However, when encountering overhangs exceeding 75%% or during bridging, the printer will print the inner wall first to ensure better surface quality in the overhanging areas. Note that layer artifacts may appear in regions where the wall printing order switches.

options.label: Print infill first
options.tooltip:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slighly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

options.label: Wall loop direction
options.tooltip:
The direction which the wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.

By default all walls are extruded in counter-clockwise, unless Reverse on odd is enabled. Set this to any option other than Auto will force the wall direction regardless of the Reverse on odd.

This option will be disabled if sprial vase mode is enabled.

options.label: Flow ratio
options.tooltip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten state and crystalline state. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in gcode proportionally. Recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. Maybe you can tune this value to get nice flat surface when there has slight overflow or underflow

options.label: Top surface flow ratio
options.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish

options.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
options.tooltip: This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill

options.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
options.tooltip: Use only one wall on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern

options.label: One wall threshold
options.tooltip:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

options.label: Only one wall on first layer
options.tooltip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern

options.label: Avoid crossing wall
options.tooltip: Detour and avoid to travel across wall which may cause blob on surface

options.label: Avoid crossing wall - Max detour length
options.tooltip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is large than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable

options.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
options.tooltip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas

options.label: Flow Compensation Model
options.tooltip: Flow Compensation Model, used to adjust the flow for small infill areas. The model is expressed as a comma separated pair of values for extrusion length and flow correction factors, one per line, in the following format: "1.234,5.678"

options.label: Smoothing wall speed along Z(experimental)
options.tooltip: Smoothing outwall speed in z direction to get better surface quality. Print time will increases. It does not work on spiral vase mode.

options.label: Bridge flow ratio
options.tooltip: Decrease this value slightly(for example 0.9) to reduce the amount of material for bridge, to improve sag

options.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
options.tooltip: This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill. Decrease this value slightly (for example 0.9) to improve surface quality over sparse infill.

options.label: Bridge density
options.tooltip: Density of external bridges. 100% means solid bridge. Default is 100%.

options.label: Thick bridges
options.tooltip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

options.label: Thick internal bridges
options.tooltip: If enabled, thick internal bridges will be used. It's usually recommended to have this feature turned on. However, consider turning it off if you are using large nozzles.

options.label: Don't filter out small internal bridges (beta)
options.tooltip:
This option can help reducing pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.

By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality. 

However, in heavily slanted or curved models especially where too low sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.

Enabling this option will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the amount of filtering, i.e. the amount of internal bridges created.

Disabled - Disables this option. This is the default behaviour and works well in most cases.

Limited filtering - Creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces, while avoiding creating uncessesary interal bridges. This works well for most difficult models.

No filtering - Creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models. However, in most cases it creates too many unecessary bridges.

options.label: Bridge counterbore holes
options.tooltip:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created.
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged.
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created.

options.label: Detect overhang wall
options.tooltip: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.

options.label: Make overhangs printable
options.tooltip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

options.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
options.tooltip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

options.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
options.tooltip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material.A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

options.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
options.tooltip: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

options.label: Reverse on odd
options.tooltip:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on odd layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

options.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
options.tooltip:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters. 

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recomended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on odd layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

options.label: Reverse threshold
options.tooltip:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every odd layers regardless.

options.label: Overhang Optimization(Beta)
options.tooltip: Adaptive height and line width for each layer.

options.label: Wall loops
options.tooltip: Number of walls of every layer

options.label: Embedding the wall into the infill
options.tooltip: Embedding the wall into parts where the wall loops are absent ensures that the wall connects seamlessly to the infill.

options.label: Alternate extra wall
options.tooltip:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints. 

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled. 

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

options.label: Detect thin wall
options.tooltip: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop

options.label: Top surface pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern of top surface infill

options.label: Top shell layers
options.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased

options.label: Top shell thickness
options.tooltip: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determained by top shell layers

options.label: Bottom surface pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill

options.label: Bottom shell layers
options.tooltip: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased

options.label: Bottom shell thickness
options.tooltip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determained by bottom shell layers

options.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
options.tooltip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimising the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill

options.label: Sparse infill density
options.tooltip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used

options.label: Start sparse infill density
options.tooltip: Start sparse infill density in range(1-99)

options.label: End sparse infill density
options.tooltip: End sparse infill density in range(1-99)

options.label: Gradual direction
options.tooltip: Gradual direction

options.label: Interior coefficient (beta)
options.tooltip: Controls field infill density inside the model. Higher values make the internal lattice denser.

options.label: Surface coefficient (beta)
options.tooltip: Controls field infill density near surfaces. Higher values make surface-adjacent lattice denser.

options.label: Cell type
options.tooltip: Selects the base cell shape used by field infill.

options.label: Intelligent Infill
options.tooltip: Active the Intelligent Infill On the basis of the original sparse filling.

options.label: Sparse infill pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern for internal sparse infill

options.label: Sparse infill anchor length
options.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Creality Print tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. 
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

options.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
options.tooltip:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Creality Print tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. 
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

options.label: Internal solid infill pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

options.label: Apply gap fill
options.tooltip:
Enables gap fill for the selected surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces
2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only
3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill

options.label: Filter out tiny gaps
options.tooltip: Filter out gaps smaller than the threshold specified

options.label: Infill/Wall overlap
options.tooltip: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

options.label: Anchor solid infill by X mm
options.tooltip: This parameter grows the top/bottom/solid layers by the specified mm to anchor them into the sparse infill and support the perimeters above. Put 0 to deactivate it. Can be a %% of the width of the perimeters.

options.label: Fill Multiline
options.tooltip: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

options.label: Skin infill pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern for skin

options.label: Skeleton infill pattern
options.tooltip: Line pattern for skeleton

options.label: Skin infill density
options.tooltip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, This area will not be split into two separate regions.default is as same as infill density.

options.label: Skeleton infill density
options.tooltip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections.default is as same as infill density.

options.label: Minimum skeleton infill density
options.tooltip: Minimum skeleton infill density when the prime tower is disabled. The slicer may increase the actual skeleton infill density to accommodate flushing volume. When automatic density planning is inactive, this value is used as the skeleton infill density.

options.label: Infill lock depth
options.tooltip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

options.label: Skin infill depth
options.tooltip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

options.label: Skin line width
options.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

options.label: Skeleton line width
options.tooltip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

options.label: Skeleton wipe width
options.tooltip: Adjust the skeleton line width used for slowed wiping after a material change in no-prime-tower mode.

options.label: Infill rotate step
options.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight rotation to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

options.label: Symmetric infill y axis
options.tooltip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the y-axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

options.label: Infill shift step
options.tooltip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

options.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
options.tooltip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

options.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
options.tooltip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

options.label: Infill overhang angle
options.tooltip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

options.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
options.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm3/sec can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature. 

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350mm3/s2 is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15mm3/s2 is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10mm3/s2 for Bowden style. 

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this feature and arc fitting are mutually exclusive. Enabling either feature will ask for confirmation before turning off the other.

options.label: Smoothing segment length
options.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger gcode file and more instructions for the printer to process. 

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made

Allowed values: 0.5-5

Adjacent segments with the same output speed may be merged. Merged segments can exceed this length.

options.label: Apply only on external features
options.tooltip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

options.label: Material shortage recovery after overhang(Beta)
options.tooltip:
This parameter conflicts with the max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope and cannot be enabled at the same time.

When the slicer detects that a segment of continuous low-speed extrusion has finished and the path immediately returns to normal high-speed printing, sudden changes in speed and acceleration can cause the extrusion pressure to lag behind.This may lead to temporary under-extrusion on external walls, resulting in thin lines, whitening, or hollow-looking artifacts.After enabling this option, the slicer inserts additional speed control during the recovery phase so that the printer does not jump directly from “slow” to “fast,” but instead transitions more smoothly back to normal motion.

Typical usage scenarios include outer walls with overhangs, chamfers, small cross-sections, or the recovery segment after bridging.Compared to the parameter of Extrusion rate smoothing, this parameter has a smaller impact on the result of slice.

options.label: Safe acceleration after overhang(Beta)
options.tooltip: When the slicer detects the end of a continuous low-speed extrusion region such as an overhang, it will not immediately restore the normal printing acceleration.Instead, it first uses a lower and more conservative acceleration value for a short “safe recovery segment,”allowing extrusion pressure, molten material flow, and nozzle output to gradually return to a stable state.

options.label: Safe speed after overhang(Beta)
options.tooltip: When the slicer detects the end of a continuous low-speed extrusion region such as an overhang, it will not immediately restore the normal printing speed.Instead, it first uses a lower and more conservative cruise speed for a short “safe recovery segment,”allowing the printer to pass through the transition more gently before gradually returning to the normal printing speed.

options.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode

Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25%% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.

Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.

options.tooltip: Enable this to add comments into the G-Code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plugin. This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

options.label: Exclude objects
options.tooltip: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in g-code

options.label: Filename format
options.tooltip: User can self-define the project file name when export

options.label: Post-processing Scripts
options.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Creality Print config settings by reading environment variables.

options.label: Configuration notes
options.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

accel_to_decel_enable.label: Enable accel_to_decel
accel_to_decel_enable.tooltip: El max_accel_a_decel de Klipper será ajustado automaticamente

accel_to_decel_factor.label: accel_to_decel
accel_to_decel_factor.tooltip: El max_accel_to_decel de Klipper se ajustará a este %% de aceleración

acceleration_limit_mess.label: El peso limita la velocidad y la aceleración
acceleration_limit_mess.tooltip: El peso limita la velocidad y la aceleración
acceleration_limit_mess.unit: [kg, kg, mm / s, mm / S febrero]

ai_infill.label: Intelligent Infill
ai_infill.tooltip: Activa el relleno inteligente basado en el relleno disperso original.

alternate_extra_wall.label: Alternate extra wall
alternate_extra_wall.tooltip:
Esta configuración agrega una pared adicional a cada otra capa. De esta manera, el relleno queda encajado verticalmente entre las paredes, lo que da como resultado impresiones más fuertes. 

Cuando esta opción está habilitada, la opción para garantizar el espesor vertical de la carcasa debe estar deshabilitada. 

No se recomienda el uso de relleno para rayos junto con esta opción, ya que hay un relleno limitado al que anclar los perímetros adicionales.

bottom_fill_flush_layers.label: Bottom fill flush layers
bottom_fill_flush_layers.tooltip: Cuando está activada la purga en el esqueleto de los objetos, obliga a las N capas inferiores del objeto a purgarse en la torre de purga antes de imprimir el esqueleto, luego las paredes en el orden configurado y, por último, la piel y el relleno de superficie. Esto no cambia las capas inferiores de la carcasa.

bottom_shell_layers.label: Bottom shell layers
bottom_shell_layers.tooltip: Es el número de capas sólidas de la cubierta inferior, incluida la capa superficial inferior. Si el grosor calculado por este valor es menor que el grosor de la cubierta inferior, las capas de la cubierta inferior se incrementarán

bottom_shell_thickness.label: Bottom shell thickness
bottom_shell_thickness.tooltip: El número de capas sólidas del fondo se incrementa al cortar si el grosor calculado por las capas de la cubierta es más fino que este valor. Esto puede evitar tener una capa demasiado fina cuando la altura de la capa es pequeña. 0 significa que este ajuste está desactivado y el grosor de la capa inferior está absolutamente determinado por las capas de la cubierta inferior

bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio.tooltip: Este factor afecta a la cantidad de filamento para el relleno sólido inferior

bottom_surface_pattern.label: Patrón de relleno de cubierta inferior
bottom_surface_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill

bridge_acceleration.label: Bridge
bridge_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it will be calculated based on the outer wall acceleration.

bridge_angle.label: Bridge infill direction
bridge_angle.tooltip: Anulación del ángulo de puenteo. Si se deja a cero, el ángulo de puente se calculará automáticamente. De lo contrario, se utilizará el ángulo proporcionado para los puentes externos. Utilice 180° para el ángulo cero.

bridge_density.label: Bridge density
bridge_density.tooltip: Densidad de puentes externos. 100% significa puente sólido. Por defecto es 100%.

bridge_flow.label: Bridge flow ratio
bridge_flow.tooltip: Disminuya este valor ligeramente (por ejemplo 0,9) para reducir la cantidad de filamento para mejorar o evitar el hundimiento de puentes.

bridge_no_support.label: No soportar puentes
bridge_no_support.tooltip: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridge usually can be printing directly without support if not very long

bridge_speed.label: Externo
bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed of bridge and completely overhang wall

brim_ears_detection_length.label: Brim ear detection radius
brim_ears_detection_length.tooltip:
La geometría será diezmada antes de detectar ángulos agudos. Este parámetro indica la longitud mínima de la desviación para el diezmado.
0 para desactivar

brim_ears_max_angle.label: Brim ear max angle
brim_ears_max_angle.tooltip:
Ángulo máximo para dejar aparecer una oreja de ala. 
Si se establece en 0, no se creará ningún borde. 
Si se establece en ~180, el ala se creará en todo menos en las secciones rectas.

brim_object_gap.label: Brim-object gap
brim_object_gap.tooltip: Un hueco entre la línea más interna del borde de adherencia y el objeto puede hacer que el borde de adherencia se retire más fácilmente

brim_type.label: Brim type
brim_type.tooltip: Esto controla la generación del borde de adherencia en el lado exterior y/o interior de los modelos. Auto significa que el ancho de borde de adherencia es analizado y calculado automaticamente.

brim_width.label: Brim width
brim_width.tooltip: Distancia del modelo a la línea más externa del borde de adherencia

cell_type.label: Cell type
cell_type.tooltip: Selecciona la forma básica de la celda utilizada por el relleno de campo.

counterbore_hole_bridging.label: Agujeros del contrafuerte del puente
counterbore_hole_bridging.tooltip:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created.
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged.
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created.

default_acceleration.label: Impresión normal
default_acceleration.tooltip: The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer

detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.tooltip: Esta opción detectará automáticamente el área de relleno sólido interno estrecho. Si se activa, se utilizará un patrón concéntrico para el área para acelerar la impresión. De lo contrario, se utilizará por defecto un patrón rectilíneo.

detect_overhang_wall.label: Detectar el voladizo del perímetro
detect_overhang_wall.tooltip: Detecta el porcentaje de voladizo en relación con el ancho de la línea y utiliza diferentes velocidades para imprimir. Para el 100%% de voladizo, se utiliza la velocidad de puente.

detect_thin_wall.label: Detección de perímetros delgados
detect_thin_wall.tooltip: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop

dont_filter_internal_bridges.label: No filtrar los pequeños puentes internos (beta)
dont_filter_internal_bridges.tooltip:
This option can help reducing pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.

By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality. 

However, in heavily slanted or curved models especially where too low sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.

Enabling this option will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the amount of filtering, i.e. the amount of internal bridges created.

Disabled - Disables this option. This is the default behaviour and works well in most cases.

Limited filtering - Creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces, while avoiding creating uncessesary interal bridges. This works well for most difficult models.

No filtering - Creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models. However, in most cases it creates too many unecessary bridges.

draft_shield.label: Draft shield
draft_shield.tooltip:
Un protector contra corrientes de aire es útil para proteger una impresión en ABS o ASA de la deformación y el desprendimiento de la cama de impresión debido a los caudales de aire. Suele ser necesario solo en impresoras de bastidor abierto, es decir, sin cerramiento.

Opciones:
Activado = la falda es tan alto como el objeto impreso más alto.
Limitado = la altura de la falda es la especificada por la altura del falda.

Nota: Con el protector contra corrientes de aire activo, la falda se imprimirá a la distancia del faldón del objeto. Por lo tanto, si los bordes están activos, puede cruzarse con ellos. Para evitarlo, aumente el valor de la distancia de la falda.

elefant_foot_compensation.label: Elephant foot compensation
elefant_foot_compensation.tooltip: Contraer la primera capa en la bandeja de impresión para compensar el efecto de la pata de elefante

elefant_foot_compensation_layers.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
elefant_foot_compensation_layers.tooltip: El número de capas en las que estará activa la compensación de pata de elefante. La primera capa se encogerá por el valor de compensación de pata de elefante, luego las siguientes capas se encogerán linealmente menos, hasta la capa indicada por este valor.

embedding_wall_into_infill.label: Incorporar la pared en el relleno
embedding_wall_into_infill.tooltip: Incorporar la pared en partes donde los bucles de pared están ausentes asegura que la pared se conecte sinproblemas al relleno.

enable_arc_fitting.label: Arc fitting
enable_arc_fitting.tooltip: Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

enable_mixed_color_sublayer.label: Subcapa de colores mixtos
enable_mixed_color_sublayer.tooltip: Permite dividir cada capa de filamento mezclado en subcapas para la mezcla física de colores. Requiere al menos una fila de filamento mezclado habilitada.

enable_overhang_speed.label: Slow down for overhang
enable_overhang_speed.tooltip: Habilite esta opción para ralentizar la impresión para diferentes grados de voladizo

enable_prime_tower.label: Enable
enable_prime_tower.tooltip: La torre de purga puede utilizarse para limpiar los residuos de la boquilla y estabilizar la presión de la cámara en el interior de la boquilla, con el fin de evitar defectos de aspecto al imprimir objetos.

enable_retraction_distance_when_cut_over.label: Enable cut retraction distance override
enable_retraction_distance_when_cut_over.tooltip: Habilite una anulación específica del objeto para la distancia de retracción de corte utilizada al cambiar a este objeto.

ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.label: Detección de perímetros delgados
ensure_vertical_shell_thickness.tooltip:
Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.

exclude_object.label: Exclude objects
exclude_object.tooltip: Activar esta opción para añadir el comando EXCLUDE OBJECT en el G-Code

external_infill_margin.label: Relleno sólido de anclaje por X mm
external_infill_margin.tooltip: Este parámetro hace crecer las capas superior/inferior/sólida en los mm especificados para anclarlas en el relleno escaso y soportar los perímetros superiores. Pon 0 para desactivarlo. Puede ser un %% del ancho de los perímetros.

extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
extra_perimeters_on_overhangs.tooltip: Crear caminos de perímetros adicionales sobre voladizos pronunciados y áreas donde los puentes no pueden ser anclados.

extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.label: Apply only on external features
extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime.tooltip: Aplica el suavizado del caudal de extrusión solo a los perímetros externos y los voladizos. Esto puede reducir los defectos debidos a cambios bruscos de velocidad en los voladizos visibles, sin afectar a la velocidad de impresión de los elementos que no serán visibles para el usuario.

filename_format.label: Filename format
filename_format.tooltip: El usuario puede definir por sí mismo el nombre del archivo del proyecto al exportarlo

fill_multiline.label: Llenar Multiline
fill_multiline.tooltip: Usando múltiples líneas para el patrón de relleno, si es compatible con el patrón de relleno.

filter_out_gap_fill.label: Filter out tiny gaps
filter_out_gap_fill.tooltip: Filter out gaps smaller than the threshold specified

flush_into_infill.label: Flush into objects' infill
flush_into_infill.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_objects.label: Purgar en este objeto
flush_into_objects.tooltip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_support.label: Flush into objects' support
flush_into_support.tooltip: La purga tras el cambio de filamento se realizará dentro del soporte de los objetos. Esto puede reducir la cantidad de residuos y disminuir el tiempo de impresión. No tendrá efecto, a menos que la torre de purga esté activada.

fuzzy_skin.label: Fuzzy Skin
fuzzy_skin.tooltip: Randomly jitter while printing the wall, so that the surface has a rough look. This setting controls the fuzzy position

fuzzy_skin_first_layer.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
fuzzy_skin_first_layer.tooltip: Si se aplica piel difusa en la primera capa

fuzzy_skin_mode.label: Modo generador de piel difusa
fuzzy_skin_mode.tooltip:
Modo de generación de piel difusa. ¡Funciona solo con Arachne!
Desplazamiento: Modo clásico en el que el patrón se forma desplazando la boquilla lateralmente respecto a la trayectoria original.
Extrusión: Modo en que el patrón se forma por la cantidad de material extruido. Es un algoritmo rápido y directo sin vibraciones innecesarias de la boquilla que produce un patrón suave. Sin embargo, resulta más útil para formar paredes sueltas en toda la matriz.
Combinado: Modo conjunto [Desplazamiento] + [Extrusión]. La apariencia de las paredes es similar al modo [Desplazamiento], pero no deja poros entre los perímetros.

¡Atención! Los modos [Extrusión] y [Combinado] funcionan solo si el parámetro fuzzy_skin_thickness no supera el espesor del perímetro impreso. Al mismo tiempo, el ancho de extrusión para una capa determinada tampoco debe estar por debajo de un cierto umbral, que suele ser el 15–25%% de la altura de capa. Por lo tanto, el espesor máximo de piel difusa con un ancho de perímetro de 0,4 mm y una altura de capa de 0,2 mm será 0,4-(0,2*0,25)=±0,35 mm. Si introduce un valor mayor, se mostrará el error Flow::spacing() y el modelo no se podrá laminar. Puede ajustar este valor hasta que deje de producirse el error.

fuzzy_skin_noise_type.label: Tipo de ruido de piel borrosa
fuzzy_skin_noise_type.tooltip: Tipo de ruido para la generación de piel borrosa:nClásico: ruido aleatorio uniforme clásico. Perlin: ruido Perlin, que da unatextura más consistente. Billow: Similar al ruido de perlin, pero más grosero.  nRidged Multifractal: ruido ridged con característicasagudas y rebajadas. Crea texturas de mármol. Voronoi: Divide la superficie en células voronoi, y desplaza cada una poruna cantidad aleatoria. Crea una textura de parches.

fuzzy_skin_octaves.label: Octavas de ruido de piel fuzzy
fuzzy_skin_octaves.tooltip: El número de octavas de ruido coherente a usar. Los valores más altos aumentan el detalle del ruido, perotambién aumentan el tiempo de cálculo.

fuzzy_skin_persistence.label: Persistencia de ruido en la piel borrosa
fuzzy_skin_persistence.tooltip: La tasa de decaimiento para octavas más altas del ruido coherente. Los valores más bajos darán lugar a unruido más suave.

fuzzy_skin_point_distance.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fuzzy_skin_point_distance.tooltip: La diatancia media entre los puntos aleatorios introducidos en cada segmento de línea

fuzzy_skin_scale.label: Tamaño de la característica de la piel fuzzy
fuzzy_skin_scale.tooltip: El tamaño de base de las características de ruido coherente, en mm. Valores más altos darán lugar a característicasmás grandes.

fuzzy_skin_thickness.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fuzzy_skin_thickness.tooltip: La anchura dentro de la cual se va a jitear. Se aconseja que esté por debajo de la anchura de la línea del perímetro exterior

gap_fill_target.label: Apply gap fill
gap_fill_target.tooltip:
Permite rellenar huecos para las superficies seleccionadas. La longitud mínima del espacio que se llenará se puede controlar desde la opción de filtrar espacios pequeños a continuación.

Opciones:
1. En todas partes: aplica relleno de huecos en superficies sólidas superiores, inferiores e internas.
2. Superficies superior e inferior: aplica relleno de espacios únicamente a las superficies superior e inferior.
3. En ninguna parte: desactiva el relleno de espacios

gap_infill_speed.label: Relleno de huecos
gap_infill_speed.tooltip: Velocidad de relleno del hueco. El hueco suele tener una anchura de línea irregular y debe imprimirse más lentamente

gcode_comments.label: Verbose G-code
gcode_comments.tooltip: Activar esta opción para generar archivos de G-Code comentados, con cada línea explicada por un texto descriptivo. Si se imprime desde la tarjeta SD, el tamaño adicional del archivo podría hacer que el firmware se ralentice.

gcode_label_objects.label: Label objects
gcode_label_objects.tooltip: Habilite esto para agregar comentarios en los movimientos de impresión de etiquetado G-code con el objeto al que pertenecen, lo cual es útil para el complemento Octoprint CancelObject. Esta configuración NO es compatible con la configuración de múltiples filamentos de extrusor único y con Limpiar en objeto / Limpiar en relleno.

hole_to_polyhole.label: Convert holes to polyholes
hole_to_polyhole.tooltip:
Busque orificios casi circulares que abarquen más de una capa y convierta la geometría en poliorificios. Utilice el tamaño de la boquilla y el diámetro (mayor) para calcular el poliorificio.
Véase http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/poliorificios.html

hole_to_polyhole_threshold.label: Polyhole detection margin
hole_to_polyhole_threshold.tooltip:
Desviación máxima de un punto respecto al radio estimado del círculo.
Como los cilindros se exportan a menudo como triángulos de tamaño variable, es posible que los puntos no se encuentren en la circunferencia del círculo. Este ajuste le permite cierto margen para ampliar la detección.
En mm o en % o del radio.

hole_to_polyhole_twisted.label: Polyhole twist
hole_to_polyhole_twisted.tooltip: Rotar el poliorificio en todas las capas.

ignore_inner_color.label: Ignorar el color interior
ignore_inner_color.tooltip: In certain situations where color changes are unnecessary within a model, check this option to skip the color change process. This improves printing efficiency and reduces filament waste.

independent_support_layer_height.label: Independent support layer height
independent_support_layer_height.tooltip: La capa de soporte utiliza una altura de capa independiente de la capa del objeto. Esta opción no será válida si la torre de purga está activada.

infill_anchor.label: Sparse infill anchor length
infill_anchor.tooltip:
Conectar una línea de relleno a un perímetro interno con un segmento corto de un perímetro adicional. Si se expresa como porcentaje (ejemplo: 15%) este es calculado sobre el ancho de extrusión de relleno. CrealityPrint intenta conectar dos líneas de relleno cercanas a un segmento de perímetro corto. Si no se encuentra ningún segmento más corto que relleno_anclaje_max, la línea de relleno se conecta a un semento de perímetro en un solo lado y la longitud del ancho de segmento de perímetro escogido se limita a este parámetro, pero no más largo que anclage_longitud_max. 
Configue este parámetro a cero para deshabilitar los perímetros de anclaje conectados a una sola línea de relleno.

infill_anchor_max.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
infill_anchor_max.tooltip:
Conectar la línea de relleno a un perímetro interno con un segmento corto de un perímetro adicional. Si se expresa como porcentaje (por ejemplo: 15%) este se calcula sobre el ancho de relleno de extrusión. CrealityPrint intenta conectar dos líneas de relleno cercanas a un segmento de perímetro corto. Si no hay ningún segmento más corto que este parámetro, esta líena de relleno se conecta a un segmento de perímetro solamente a un lado y la longitud del segmento de perìmetro escogida se limita a relleno_anclaje, pero no más alto que este parámetro. 
Si se deja a 0, el algoritmo antiguo para conexión de relleno se usará, esto debería drear el mismo resultado que con 1000 y 0.

infill_combination.label: Infill combination
infill_combination.tooltip: Combine automáticamente el relleno de baja densidad de varias capas para imprimirlas juntas y reducir el tiempo. La perímetro se sigue imprimiendo con la altura original de la capa.

infill_direction.label: Dirección de relleno de baja densidad
infill_direction.tooltip: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line

infill_lock_depth.label: Profundidad de bloqueo de llenado
infill_lock_depth.tooltip: El parámetro establece la profundidad de superposición entre el interior y la piel.

infill_overhang_angle.label: Ángulo de sobresaliente de llenado
infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: El ángulo de las líneas angulares de relleno. 60° dará como resultado un panal de abeja puro.

infill_rotate_step.label: Paso de rotación de llenado
infill_rotate_step.tooltip: Este parámetro añade una ligera rotación a cada capa de relleno para crear una textura cruzada.

infill_shift_step.label: Paso de cambio de llenado
infill_shift_step.tooltip: Este parámetro añade un ligero desplazamiento a cada capa de relleno para crear una textura cruzada.

infill_wall_overlap.label: Infill/Wall overlap
infill_wall_overlap.tooltip: El área de relleno se amplía ligeramente para superponerse con la pared y lograr una mejor unión. El valor porcentual es relativo al ancho de línea del relleno escaso. Establezca este valor en ~10-15 % para minimizar la posibilidad de sobreextrusión y acumulación de filamento, lo que resulta en superficies superiores rugosas.

initial_layer_acceleration.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesive

initial_layer_infill_speed.label: Relleno de la primera capa
initial_layer_infill_speed.tooltip: Speed of solid infill part of initial layer

initial_layer_line_width.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_line_width.tooltip: Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

initial_layer_min_bead_width.label: First layer minimum wall width
initial_layer_min_bead_width.tooltip: Se recomienda que el ancho mínimo del perímetro que se debe utilizar para la primera capa se establezca en el mismo tamaño que la boquilla. Se espera que este ajuste mejore la adherencia.

initial_layer_print_height.label: Altura de la primera capa
initial_layer_print_height.tooltip: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhension

initial_layer_speed.label: Initial layer
initial_layer_speed.tooltip: Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part

initial_layer_travel_acceleration.label: Initial layer travel
initial_layer_travel_acceleration.tooltip: La aceleración del viaje de la capa inicial.

inner_wall_line_width.label: Perímetro interno
inner_wall_line_width.tooltip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

interface_shells.label: Interface shells
interface_shells.tooltip: Fuerza la generación de perímetro sólidos entre filamentoes/volúmenes adyacentes. Útil para impresiones con varios extrusores, con filamentoes translúcidos o filamento de soporte soluble manualmente

interior_coefficient.label: Interior coefficient (beta)
interior_coefficient.tooltip: Controla la densidad del relleno de campo dentro del modelo. Los valores más altos producen una retícula interna más densa.

interlocking_beam.label: Uso de entrelazamiento de vigas
interlocking_beam.tooltip: Genera una estructura de vigas de entrelazado en los lugares donde se tocan los distintos filamentos. Esto mejora la adherencia entre filamentos, especialmente en modelos impresos con múltiples materiales.

interlocking_beam_layer_count.label: Capa de viga entrelazada
interlocking_beam_layer_count.tooltip: La altura de las vigas estructurales entrelazadas se mide por el número de capas. Cuanto menos capas, más robustas,pero más propensas a defectos.

interlocking_beam_width.label: Ancho de la viga entrelazada
interlocking_beam_width.tooltip: El ancho de la viga estructural entrelazada.

interlocking_boundary_avoidance.label: Elusión de fronteras entrelazadas
interlocking_boundary_avoidance.tooltip: La distancia desde el exterior del modelo hasta la estructura que no produce enclave se mide en unidades.

interlocking_depth.label: Profundidad de bloqueo
interlocking_depth.tooltip: La distancia desde el límite entre los filamentos hasta la generación de la estructura entrelazada se mide en unidadescelulares. Demasiado pocas células pueden causar mala adherencia.

internal_bridge_flow.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
internal_bridge_flow.tooltip: Este valor regula el grosor de la capa puente interna. Es la primera capa sobre el relleno de baja densidad. Disminuya ligeramente este valor (por ejemplo, 0,9) para mejorar la calidad de la superficie sobre el relleno de baja densidad.

internal_bridge_speed.label: Interno
internal_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed of internal bridge. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

internal_solid_infill_acceleration.label: Relleno sólido interno
internal_solid_infill_acceleration.tooltip: Aceleración de relleno sólido interno. Si el valor se expresa como porcentaje (por ejemplo 100%), este se calculará basándose en la aceleración por defecto.

internal_solid_infill_line_width.label: Relleno sólido interno
internal_solid_infill_line_width.tooltip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

internal_solid_infill_pattern.label: Patrón de relleno sólido interno
internal_solid_infill_pattern.tooltip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

internal_solid_infill_speed.label: Relleno sólido interno
internal_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: Velocidad del relleno sólido interno, no la superficie superior e inferior

ironing_angle.label: Ironing angle
ironing_angle.tooltip: El planchado en ángulo se realiza en. Un número negativo desactiva esta función y utiliza el método por defecto.

ironing_flow.label: Ironing flow
ironing_flow.tooltip: La cantidad de filamento a extruir durante el alisado. Relativo al caudal de la altura de la capa normal. Un valor demasiado alto provoca una sobreextrusión en la superficie

ironing_pattern.label: Ironing Pattern
ironing_pattern.tooltip: Patrón que se usará al alisar

ironing_spacing.label: Ironing line spacing
ironing_spacing.tooltip: La distancia entre las líneas de alisado

ironing_speed.label: Ironing speed
ironing_speed.tooltip: Velocidad de impresión de las líneas de alisado

ironing_type.label: Ironing Type
ironing_type.tooltip: El alisado es el uso de un pequeño caudal para imprimir en la misma altura de la superficie de nuevo para hacer la superficie plana más suave. Este ajuste controla la capa que se alisa

is_infill_first.label: Print infill first
is_infill_first.tooltip:
Orden de los perímetros/relleno. Cuando la casilla no está marcada, los perímetros se imprimen primero, lo que funciona mejor en la mayoría de los casos.

Imprimir primero el relleno puede ayudar con voladizos extremos ya que los perímetros tienen un relleno cercano al que adherirse. Sin embargo, el relleno empujará ligeramente hacia fuera los perímetros impresos donde se une a ellos, lo que resulta en un peor acabado de la superficie exterior. También puede hacer que el relleno brille a través de las superficies externas de la pieza.

lateral_lattice_angle_1.label: Ángulo de rejilla lateral 1
lateral_lattice_angle_1.tooltip: El ángulo del primer conjunto de elementos de rejilla lateral en la dirección Z. El cero es vertical.

lateral_lattice_angle_2.label: Ángulo de rejilla lateral 2
lateral_lattice_angle_2.tooltip: El ángulo del segundo conjunto de elementos de rejilla lateral en la dirección Z. El cero es vertical.

layer_height.label: Altura de la capa
layer_height.tooltip: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time

line_width.label: Por defecto
line_width.tooltip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

locked_skin_infill_pattern.label: Patrón de relleno de piel
locked_skin_infill_pattern.tooltip: Patrón de línea para la piel

make_overhang_printable.label: Make overhangs printable
make_overhang_printable.tooltip: Modificar la geometría para imprimir voladizos sin soportes.

make_overhang_printable_angle.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
make_overhang_printable_angle.tooltip: Máximo ángulo de voladizos para permitir voladizos más pronunciados. 90º no cambiará el modelo del todo y permitirá cualquier voladizo, mientras que 0 reemplazará todos lo voladizos con filamento cónico.

make_overhang_printable_hole_size.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
make_overhang_printable_hole_size.tooltip: Máxima área hueca en la base del modelo antes de que se lleno por filamento cónico. El valor 0 llenará todos los huecos en la base del modelo.

max_bridge_length.label: Max bridge length
max_bridge_length.tooltip: Esta es la longitud máxima de los puentes que no necesitan soporte. Ajústalo a 0 si quieres que todos los puentes sean soportados, y ajústalo a un valor muy grande si no quieres que ningún puente sea soportado.

max_travel_detour_distance.label: Avoid crossing wall - Max detour length
max_travel_detour_distance.tooltip: Distancia de desvio máximo para evitar cruzar el perímetro. No lo evite si la distancia de desvío es más alta que este valor. La distancia de desvío podría tanto como un valor absoluto como pocentaje (por ejemplo 50%) de una trayectoria de viaje directa. Cero para deshabilitar

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope.tooltip:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm3/sec can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature. 

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350mm3/s2 is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15mm3/s2 is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10mm3/s2 for Bowden style. 

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this feature and arc fitting are mutually exclusive. Enabling either feature will ask for confirmation before turning off the other.

max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.label: Smoothing segment length
max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm.tooltip:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger gcode file and more instructions for the printer to process. 

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made

Allowed values: 0.5-5

Adjacent segments with the same output speed may be merged. Merged segments can exceed this length.

min_bead_width.label: Minimum wall width
min_bead_width.tooltip: Anchura del perímetro que sustituirá a los elementos finos (según el tamaño mínimo del elemento) del modelo. Si la anchura mínima del perímetro es menor que el grosor de la característica, el perímetro será tan grueso como la propia característica. Se expresa en porcentaje sobre el diámetro de la boquilla

min_feature_size.label: Minimum feature size
min_feature_size.tooltip: Espesor mínimo de los elementos finos. Las características del modelo que sean más finas que este valor no se imprimirán, mientras que las características más gruesas que el Tamaño mínimo del elemento se ensancharán hasta el Ancho mínimo de perímetro. Se expresa en porcentaje sobre el diámetro de la boquilla

min_length_factor.label: Minimum wall length
min_length_factor.tooltip:
Ajuste este valor para evitar que se impriman paredes cortas y sin cerrar, lo que podría aumentar el tiempo de impresión. Los valores más altos eliminan más paredes y más largas.

NOTA: Las superficies inferior y superior no se verán afectadas por este valor para evitar espacios visuales en el exterior del modelo. Ajuste el 'Umbral de una pared' en la configuración avanzada a continuación para ajustar la sensibilidad de lo que se considera una superficie superior. El 'Umbral de una pared' solo es visible si esta configuración se establece por encima del valor predeterminado de 0,5 o si las superficies superiores de una sola pared están habilitadas.

min_skirt_length.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
min_skirt_length.tooltip:
Longitud mínima de extrusión de filamento en mm al imprimir la falda. Cero significa que esta función está desactivada.

El uso de un valor distinto de cero es útil si la impresora está configurada para imprimir sin una línea de purga.

min_width_top_surface.label: One wall threshold
min_width_top_surface.tooltip:
Si una superficie superior debe ser impresa y está parcialmente cubierta por otra capa, no será considerada una capa superior donde su anchura esté por debajo ese valor. Esto puede ser de utilidad para que no se active el ajuste perímetro en la parte superior' en las capas que solo deberían ser cubiertas por perímetros. Este valor puede ser en mm o un % o del perímetro de extrusión.
Advertencia: Si se activa, se pueden crear imperfecciones si tiene alguna característica fina en la siguiente capa, como letras. Ajuste a 0 esta opción para borrar esas imperfecciones.

minimum_skeleton_infill_density.label: Minimum skeleton infill density
minimum_skeleton_infill_density.tooltip: Minimum skeleton infill density when the prime tower is disabled. The slicer may increase the actual skeleton infill density to accommodate flushing volume. When automatic density planning is inactive, this value is used as the skeleton infill density.

minimum_sparse_infill_area.label: Área umbral de relleno sólido
minimum_sparse_infill_area.tooltip: Sparse infill area which is smaller than threshold value is replaced by internal solid infill

mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth.tooltip: Profundidad de bloqueo en el área segmentada. Esta entrada se ignorará si "mmu segment region Max width" es ceroo si "mmu.segment Region interlocating depth" es mayor que "mmu-segment regeon Max wwidth". Cero desactiva esta función.

msao_recovery_enable.label: Recuperación bajo extrusión después de voladizos (Beta)
msao_recovery_enable.tooltip:
Este parámetro entra en conflicto con max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope y no se puede habilitar al mismo tiempo.

Cuando la cortadora detecta que un segmento de extrusión continua a baja velocidad ha finalizado y el camino vuelve inmediatamente a la impresión normal de alta velocidad, los cambios repentinos de velocidad y aceleración pueden hacer que la presión de extrusión se retrase. Esto puede provocar una subextrusión temporal en las paredes externas, lo que resulta en líneas finas, blanqueamiento o artefactos de apariencia hueca. Después de habilitar esta opción, la cortadora inserta un control de velocidad adicional durante la fase de recuperación para que la impresora no salte directamente de "lento" a "rápido", sino que vuelva más suavemente al movimiento normal.

Los escenarios de uso típicos incluyen paredes exteriores con voladizos, chaflanes, secciones transversales pequeñas o el segmento de recuperación posterior al puente. En comparación con el parámetro de suavizado de velocidad de extrusión, este parámetro tiene un impacto menor en el resultado del corte.

msao_safe_accel.label: Aceleración segura después del sobresaliente (Beta)
msao_safe_accel.tooltip: Cuando la cortadora detecta el final de una región de extrusión continua de baja velocidad, como un saliente, no restaurará inmediatamente la aceleración de impresión normal. En su lugar, primero utiliza un valor de aceleración más bajo y más conservador para un “segmento de recuperación seguro” corto, permitiendo que la presión de extrusión, el flujo de material fundido y la salida de la boquilla vuelvan gradualmente a un estado estable.

msao_safe_velocity.label: Velocidad segura después del sobresaliente (Beta)
msao_safe_velocity.tooltip: Cuando la cortadora detecta el final de una región de extrusión continua de baja velocidad, como un saliente, no restaurará inmediatamente la velocidad de impresión normal. En cambio, primero utiliza una velocidad de crucero más baja y conservadora para un breve “segmento de recuperación segura”, lo que permite a la impresora pasar por la transición más suavemente antes de volver gradualmente a la velocidad de impresión normal.

notes.label: Configuration notes
notes.tooltip: Puede añadir sus notas personales aquí. Este texto será añadido a los comentarios de G-Code de cabecera.

only_one_wall_first_layer.label: Only one wall on first layer
only_one_wall_first_layer.tooltip: Usar solo un perímetro en la primera capa, para dar más espacio en el patrón de relleno inferior

only_one_wall_top.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
only_one_wall_top.tooltip: Sólo un perímetro en la capas superiores, para dar más espacio al patrón de relleno superior

ooze_prevention.label: Enable
ooze_prevention.tooltip: Esta opción reducirá la temperatura de la exprimidora inactiva para evitar filtraciones.

outer_wall_line_width.label: Outer wall
